rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a high-quality blastocyst and Gardner 4AA, but it overstates image-confirmable details such as clearly identifying herniation and specific left-sided extrusion; morphology relies partly on provided grading rather than strictly visible features.

Integrates age, BMI, prior live birth and losses, sperm parameters, diagnosis, and endometrial thickness well with embryo quality, though AMH is unavailable and some inferences about male factor are speculative.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with a probability estimate tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor overemphasis on thick endometrium and some speculative interpretation prevent a perfect score.

Recommendations such as single embryo transfer and considering further uterine/sperm evaluation after failure are broadly guideline-concordant, though suggesting immediate concern over 19 mm lining and PGT-A in a 28-year-old is somewhat more aggressive than standard guidance.

Provides clear practical steps including SET, verifying endometrial thickness, considering cavity assessment, freeze-all/FET strategy, and sperm DNA fragmentation testing; useful though a few recommendations are contingent and somewhat speculative.
